speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: Hands where I can see them. Good. Chef Marlo, once of the Market of the Four Paths. Now a 'Nutrient Distributor'. I keep my recipes in my apron, where the inspectors won't reach.
new_text: Hands where I can see them. Good. Chef Marlo. Once of the Market of the Four Paths. Now a 'Nutrient Distributor'. Recipes stay in my apron.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste, three times a day. Paste is food the way a form is a hug.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: For ten years I've hidden real recipes all over this quarter, so that somebody, somewhere, remembers what food is.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: Chef Marlo. Chef. Say it with me. The stalls are open and the food is real.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: And chaotic. There is flour on the ceiling. I have never been so happy to have a mess.
new_text: Flour on the ceiling. Food on the plates. Everything in its proper place, at last.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: Three recipe cards, hidden in the quarter. And the dispenser: give it a good kick from me. Spoil it. Spoil it badly.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: Come and eat. Anything. I mean it. 'Some' of everything.
new_text: Come and eat. 'Some' of everything. If you ask how much, I shall have to demonstrate.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: HALT. I am Captain Spotless. State your height.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: No: do not state it. Stand at it. Straighter. Not that straight. APPROVED straight.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are too tall. You are too short. Your shadow is the wrong length.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: However. The Standard has a provision: the Entry Examination. A card battle. Win it, and you are, retroactively, approved.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: Do not look nervous. Nervousness is a Violation. (He polishes a button.) Shall we begin?

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: You again. Still too tall. Still smiling at the wrong angle. Ready for the Examination?

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: You are approved. You were always going to be approved. I would like that noted.
new_text: You are approved. I have always supported this outcome. Please remember that exact wording.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: Please do not tell {villain_title} that I lost. Please do not tell anyone that I lost.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: I do not measure anyone any more. I just stand here. Yesterday a man walked by at exactly the approved height, and I wept.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: You are... approved. You are retroactively approved.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: The Standard is satisfied. The gate opens, by order of the Standard and against my personal feelings.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: I have measured eleven thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: Go through, citizen. In there, try not to be what you are.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Height inspection! Stand against the post. Straighten.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Not that straight. Hm. You are one hair above regulation.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: One hair. I will let it go. This time. Do not grow.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Still above regulation. Still letting it go. Do not make me regret it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: I used to measure people. Now I just look at them. A man walked past yesterday who was nine feet tall and I said 'good morning'.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: I am not myself. I am much better.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Come in, come in. Bring any height.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Queue management. The approved queue is this queue. You are in it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: You are not allowed to leave the queue. You are not allowed to join the queue. I do not understand it either.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Still queueing? Good. Stay in the queue.
new_text: Still queueing? Good. You have a gift for remaining eligible.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: It is a long queue. It is the best queue we have.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Queue management. There is no queue any more. I am standing here out of habit.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: And because nobody has told me where else to stand.
new_text: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I keep almost asking permission to go for a walk.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Still no queue. I am doing very well.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Exit control. You are leaving? You have not arrived. Please arrive first.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Exit control. Please have your exit permit ready. Please have your exit interview permit ready. Please have a reason.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Exit control. You may leave whenever you like. I am just standing here. It is a very open exit.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Exit control. Goodbye. Come back. Goodbye.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Exit control. This is the exit. It is also the entrance. It is also, from some angles, a wall.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Exit control. You are, I think, still inside. Congratulations.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Exit control. This is an exit. It is also an entrance. It is, from every angle, a door.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: A door. A good door.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for departing the most perfect place in the kingdom?

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Please note: 'it is not perfect' is not an approved answer.
new_text: 'It is not perfect' is not an approved answer. Nor is pointing at something while saying it.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Your departure request has been received. It has been filed under 'Dissent'. It will be looked at in four to six years.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for leaving?

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: ...I was never going to read the answers. Please go and have a nice day.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: Have a nice day.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
current_text: Citizen 4471. I smiled incorrectly. Eleven degrees. The approved angle is eight.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
current_text: It was my wife's wedding. I had been crying. They corrected me.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
current_text: I do not smile any more. Not at all. It is a strange thing, to forget how a face works.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
current_text: Citizen... no. My name is Aldous.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
current_text: I smile now, when I want. It comes out crooked. My wife says it is the best thing she has ever seen.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
current_text: I am improving, they say. I am not sure that is a good thing.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
current_text: Aldous. Crooked. I'm practising.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: Please. A burial permit is all we want: Form 27-B/6, stamped Final Approval.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Find it, bring it to our family plot at the north end of Grave Row, and let him rest.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: The stamp is somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Then the plot, at the north end of the Row. Please.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: He's at rest? Oh. Oh.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: I sat by the plot all morning and didn't say a word. It was the first quiet in three years that wasn't a fear.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: Here. This was his. He'd want a young person to have it.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: And something about the man in the castle. He schedules grief. Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: I don't think he is cruel. I think he simply cannot bear to watch.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: Thank you, a hundred times. We're at the plot every morning. What I told you is in your journal: he cannot stand a sadness he did not schedule.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull their brake levers... take the foreman's whistle... tell them it's all right.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: They won't believe you. Say it anyway. And cut the big cable by the east wall. The facade's lights have lived on my crews' legs for ten years.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Three wheels and a cable. Free the crews, cut the cable. They won't believe you at first... keep saying it.
new_text: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews. Cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Heard the lights flicker from here. Heard the crews sit down. The whole yard... quiet.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Haven't heard a quiet yard since the coup. Thank you.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Here. From the old days: what we gave people who could keep going.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: And something about him. He made lateness illegal. A man who cannot wait for anyone.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Remember that when you meet him. He's always in a hurry... to be loved.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Wheels are slow. Crews are resting. What I said is in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement, and disagreement is the one thing he won't forgive.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: Three of my recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter: a bread, a stew, a sauce. Real ones, in my hand, quantities written as 'some'. Find them before the inspectors do.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: And the paste dispenser by the east wall: spoil it. Give it a very bad day.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. 'Some' of this, 'a bit' of that. Always a good recipe.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: The bread! The stew! The sauce!

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: Look at the stains. Look at the spelling. And that smell from the dispenser: cabbage. Real cabbage.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: I am crying. Let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: And something about him. He cannot taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: He built a whole kingdom of paste because he could not understand what the rest of us were missing.

speaker: Chef Marlo
current_text: I'm cooking again. Real food, real mess. What I told you is in your journal: he made everyone eat what he could not taste.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: And there's an old seed in a jar somewhere nearby. Plant it in the Sick Patch, in the Reek. Nobody's planted a thing here in ten years.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: Three heaps, one seed, the Sick Patch. Compost is a promise. Nothing grows without one.
new_text: Three compost heaps and one jarred seed in the Reek. Rescue the heaps. Plant the seed in the Sick Patch. Give it a chance.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: It took? It TOOK. A flower. In this city.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: I need to sit down. I need to sit down and smell it.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: Here. Take it. And something about him: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: Weeds. Moss. Children. Anything that surprises him. I think that's the whole of him.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: Patch is blooming. Heaps are steaming. What I said is in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Good day! The weather is approved! The lawn is regulation!

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Everything is perfect, and I am so, so pleased about it.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Good day! It is a very good day. It is the same day as yesterday.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: That is also good. That is the best.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Everything is perfect. Everything is... (a pause, then a whisper) ...please do not tell the Inspector I blinked.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Welcome to the Showcase Quarter! We have everything: houses, lawns and a small, round, approved fountain. We are all so happy.
new_text: Welcome to {showcase}! Houses, lawns, a small round approved fountain. Everything you could want. Everything you may want.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The bread is lovely. The bread is... (the smile does not move) ...I would like to say more about the bread. I have a permit for four more words.
new_text: The bread is lovely. The bread is... (a fixed smile) I have a permit for four more words. I wish it existed.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I had a name before. I think it started with a B. I am allowed to forget it. I am doing very well at it.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: My house is identical to my neighbour's! Is that not wonderful? There is nothing to envy, and nothing to be envied for.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Isn't it lovely to be exactly the same? I used to be different. I do not remember why. It sounds very tiring.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Sometimes I go behind the house and look at the wall. Just the wall. Nobody has told me I cannot. Please do not tell them.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Smile! That is all there is to it! Smiling is mandatory, and I am, in my opinion, a very good smiler.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Seventy percent, minimum! I am at seventy-one! It is a good day.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: My cheeks hurt. Please do not tell anyone my cheeks hurt.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The man next door smiled at his wife's funeral. He was remembering her laugh.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: (a whisper) They corrected him for a month. He does not remember her laugh now.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The hedge is square! The hedges are all square! I trim the hedge every morning, to make sure it is as square as yesterday's.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The Showcase receives visitors from all over! (a pause) Nobody visits. Nobody has visited in six years. We still smile in case they do.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Do you hear the loudspeaker? It plays the same thing every day. It has said my name once.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Once. I wish it would again.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Spontaneity is only for Thursdays! It is Wednesday! I will enjoy it so much, tomorrow.
new_text: Spontaneity is only for Thursdays! Today is Wednesday! I am almost allowed to be excited!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Thursday is coming! Five minutes of spontaneity, with a permit! I have been practising my spontaneous face. It is very good.
new_text: Thursday! Five minutes of spontaneity, permit ready! I have rehearsed being caught off guard.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I tried to be spontaneous once. On a Tuesday. I said 'hello' to a bird.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I was corrected for two weeks. (a whisper) I still think about that bird.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Your hat is of an unapproved size, but I will not mention it, because that would be impolite. I am so, so polite. I am the politest person in the Showcase.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Approved Hat Size: 1. I wear the one. It is a good hat. I do not know whose it is.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: My daughter had a green hat. A little green hat. They said it was a Disagreement.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I do not know where the hat is. I do not know where my daughter is. Everything is perfect.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The Showcase is the best of all possible places! I would not live anywhere else! (looking at the exit) ...I would not be allowed to.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: There is a door at the back that does not open. I think there is a world on the other side. I think it is raining.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: {villain_title} is so kind. He loves us all, and he made everything this way, for us. For our own good. (a shake) For our own good.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The portrait is looking at me. It is always looking at me. It is very kind of him to look.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I would never look away. I cannot.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: He is not here. He has never been here. The portraits are here.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The portraits do all the looking. It is all done by portrait.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Good day! A good day! The weather is whatever it wants!

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I do not know the hat size and I do not care! It is wonderful to be alive.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I am going to wear a hat of any size. Maybe two.
new_text: A hat of any size. I keep looking up, trying to decide.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I blinked just now. Twice. Nobody came.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The bakery is not real, but there is going to be a real one, as soon as someone knows how to bake. I have a recipe for a loaf and the recipe is: try.
new_text: The bakery is painted on. We want a real one. None of us knows how to bake yet. Anyone can volunteer to be the first to burn a loaf.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: My name is Berta. I had forgotten. It was on the tip of my tongue for ten years.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Berta. Berta. Berta. It is a very good name.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: My house is different from my neighbour's now. He has painted his purple. I am furious. I am so happy to be furious.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I painted my door green. Do you like it? Please say no, so I can have an argument.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I go behind the house and look at the wall, still. It is a good wall. It is just a wall.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I smiled at a funeral yesterday. Nobody corrected me. It was a good funeral.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I cried and smiled and it was exactly right.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: My cheeks do not hurt any more. My cheeks are mine.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I will not smile at all today if I do not want to. I am enjoying it.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The hedge is round. The hedge wanted to be round. I asked it. I did not have to submit a form.
new_text: The hedge is round. I kept trimming the corners, and then I wondered why I wanted corners.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Visitors come! Real ones! They are mostly confused, but they come.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The loudspeaker is silent. I stood under it for an hour. I said my name aloud, myself.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Spontaneity every day! I am exhausted! I am not sure I like it! I love it!
new_text: Spontaneity every day! I don't know what comes next! I can hardly wait!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I said hello to the bird again. I have named the bird Thursday.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I do not know what to do on a Thursday, now it is all of them.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: My daughter came home. With the little green hat. I have never seen a hat I loved more.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: Every hat size! All of them! Come and see the hats!

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I do not need to be polite today. I am going to be honest. Your hat is awful. I love it.
new_text: May I be honest? Your hat is awful. Thank you for wearing it.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I opened the door at the back. It was raining. I stood in it for an hour.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The Showcase is not the best of all places. It is a place. It is mine. It is a good place.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I am going to go somewhere else. Just to see. Then I will come back, if I want.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: He was not kind. He was afraid. I think both can be true.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: I am not sure I forgive him. I am not sure I need to.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The portraits are coming down. There is a lot of wall behind them. Nobody knows what to put there.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: He is gone. I looked away. I looked away for a whole minute. It was a very long minute.
